'''Olivia Caramello''' is an Italian [[mathematician]]. She is an associate professor at the [[University of Insubria]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uninsubria.eu/hpp/olivia.caramello|title=CARAMELLO OLIVIA Professore Associato DIPARTIMENTO DI SCIENZA E ALTA TECNOLOGIA}}</ref> in [[Como, Italy]]. She is known for her work in [[topos|topos theory]] and for pioneering the technique of toposes as bridges. She authored the 2017 book ''Theories, Sites, Toposes: Relating and studying mathematical theories through topos-theoretic bridges''.<ref>Review of ''Theories, Sites, Toposes'': Andrzej Wiśnicki, {{MR|3752150}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/theories-sites-toposes|title=Theories, Sites, Toposes|access-date=2021-03-27|archive-date=2021-03-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306110023/https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/theories-sites-toposes|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education and early career==
Caramello earned her bachelor's degree in mathematics at the [[University of Turin]] and her Diploma in Piano at the Conservatorio di Cuneo<ref>{{cite web|url=https://imaginariopuro.wordpress.com/tag/olivia-caramello/ |title=Construindo novas pontes na mathematica}}</ref> at the age of 19.

In 2009, she obtained her Ph.D. in Mathematics at the [[University of Cambridge]] (UK), as a Prince of Wales Student of Trinity College, with a thesis entitled "The duality between Grothendieck toposes and geometric theories" under the supervision of [[Peter Johnstone (mathematician)|Peter Johnstone]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=143377|title=Olivia Caramello|access-date=2021-03-21|website=Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> In 2016, she obtained her Habilitation at [[Paris Diderot University]] with a habilitation thesis entitled "Grothendieck toposes as unifying bridges in Mathematics".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oliviacaramello.com/Unification/HDROliviaCaramello.pdf|title=Grothendieck toposes as unifying 'bridges' in mathematics}}.</ref>

Caramello has held a research fellowship at Jesus College, Cambridge and post-doctoral appointments at the De Giorgi Center of the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa, Paris Diderot University and the University of Milan (as holder of a Marie Curie Fellowship of the [[Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica Francesco Severi|Istituto Nazionale di Alta Matematica]]) and the Institut des Hautes Etudes Scientifiques.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ihes.fr/en/|title=IHES, Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques Université Paris-Saclay}}</ref>

==Work==
Caramello developed the theory of "toposes as bridges", which consists in methods and techniques for unifying different mathematical theories and transferring information between them by using toposes. This theory is based on the duality of [[grothendieck topology|sites]] and [[topos|Grothendieck toposes]], and on the notion of [[classifying topos]] of a geometric [[first-order logic|first-order theory]], exploiting the diversity of possible presentations of each topos by infinitely many sites or theories. Caramello's theory involves several components: on the one hand, establishing [[equivalence of categories|equivalences]] between [[topos]]es presented in different ways; on the other hand, calculating or expressing topos invariants in terms of the various types of presentations considered, in order to produce correspondences between properties or elements of these various presentations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oliviacaramello.com/Unification/HDROliviaCaramello.pdf|title=Grothendieck toposes as unifying 'bridges' in Mathematics}}</ref><ref>{{citation|last=Caramello|first=Olivia|year=2017|title=Theories, Sites, Toposes: Relating and studying mathematical theories through topos-theoretic bridges|publisher=Oxford University Press|url=
https://global.oup.com/academic/product/theories-sites-toposes-9780198758914?cc=gb&lang=en}}</ref>

The theory of "toposes as bridges" can be considered a meta-mathematical theory of the relations between different theories<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.laurentlafforgue.org/math/TheorieCaramello.pdf|title=La th ́eorie de Caramello : un cadre en construction pour des correspondances du type de celle de Langlands ?|access-date=2021-03-21}}</ref> and her program contributes to realizing the unifying potential of the notion of topos already glimpsed by [[Alexander Grothendieck]].<ref>{{citation|last=Caramello|first=Olivia|year=2018|title=La "notion unificatrice" de topos - Olivia Caramello, YouTube talk|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RcpZm7-S4gI&t=4588s}}</ref>

Caramello organized international conferences in topos theory, "Topos à l'IHES" (2015).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ihes.fr/en/topos-a-lihes-2/|title=Topos à l'IHES|year=2015}}</ref> and "Toposes in Como" (2018)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tcsc.lakecomoschool.org/|title=Toposes in Como|year=2018}}</ref> She is an editor of the journal ''[[Logica Universalis]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/11787/editors|title=Editors of Logica Universalis}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> and is running a blog and forum about toposes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aroundtoposes.com/|title=Around Toposes, A blog and forum about toposes, 'bridges' and the unification programme}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
Caramello was awarded the AILA<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ailalogica.it/|title=Associazione Italiana di Logica e sue Applicazioni}}</ref> (Associazione Italiana di Logica e sue Applicazioni) Prize in 2011,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://logica.dipmat.unisa.it/aila/premi/relazione-dottorato-2011.pdf|title=AILA Prize in 2011|access-date=2020-12-08|archive-date=2021-12-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206050252/http://logica.dipmat.unisa.it/aila/premi/relazione-dottorato-2011.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> a "[[L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards|L'Oréal-Unesco Fellowship for Women in Science]]" in 2014<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ihes.fr/en/institute/awards/|title=Institute Professors' Awards|publisher=IHES|access-date=2024-04-19}}</ref>  and a "Rita Levi Montalcini" position of the Italian Ministry for Education, University and Research in 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bandomontalcini.cineca.it/vincitori.php|title=Programma per Giovani Ricercatori "Rita Levi Montalcini"}}</ref>
 
Caramello's methodology of toposes as bridges has been qualified by [[André Joyal]] as a "vast extension of Felix Klein's Erlangen Programme"<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oliviacaramello.com/Unification/JoyalLetter.html|title=André Joyal's letter}}</ref> and has been endorsed by [[Fields Medal]]ists [[Alain Connes]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oliviacaramello.com/Unification/RapportSoutenanceHDROliviaCaramello.pdf|year=2016|title=Report on Habilitation Thesis by Olivia Caramello}}</ref> and [[Laurent Lafforgue]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laurentlafforgue.org/math/TheorieCaramello.pdf|title=La theorie de Caramello: un cadre en construction pour des correspondances du type de celle de Langlands?|author=Laurent Lafforgue}}</ref>

==Controversy==
In 2015 Caramello had a public controversy with a number of senior exponents of the category theory community, whom she accused of spreading negative ungrounded opinions on her work;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oliviacaramello.com/Unification/InitiativeOfClarificationResults.html|title=Unifying theory, Controversy with category theorists}}</ref> her case is discussed in an academic paper.<ref>{{citation|last1=Rittberg|first1=Colin Jakob|last2=Tanswell|first2=Fenner Stanley|last3=Van Bendegem|first3=Jean Paul|title=Epistemic injustice in mathematics|journal=Synthese|volume= 197|pages=3875–3904|year=2020|issue=9|publisher=Springer|doi=10.1007/s11229-018-01981-1|s2cid=53078904|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11229-018-01981-1}}</ref>
